question.text: As per SEBI AIF Regulations and distributor good practices, the Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) is generally expected to disclose all of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Investment strategy and target corpus of the AIF
Fee structure including management fees and expenses
A guaranteed return that the fund will deliver to investors
Risk factors associated with the fund's investment strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: The PPM disclosures the workbook covers include target corpus, investment strategy, fees and expenses, risk factors, tenure, service providers, and governance. A hurdle rate disclosed in the PPM is not the same as a guaranteed return, and distributor good practices specifically prohibit assuring returns to investors — except in the limited case of a pure debt scheme that explicitly provides assured returns in the PPM. SEBI's role at the PPM stage is to issue observations rather than to approve or guarantee performance claims. The Trap: Options A, B and D are part of standard PPM disclosures. A guaranteed-return promise is the odd one out — hurdle rate ≠ guarantee, and distributors must not assure returns outside the narrow pure-debt-PPM exception. Note: Replaced the original blanket "SEBI prohibits" / compliance-escalation language with workbook-supported wording — hurdle rates are not guaranteed returns, distributors should not assure returns except where a pure debt scheme explicitly provides assured returns in the PPM, and SEBI does not approve PPM performance claims. Keyed answer is unchanged in direction.
